traits.notes: The plant exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the shoot apex. The leaves have a characteristic appearance with prominent, curved secondary veins and a finely toothed margin. The surface is covered in fine hairs and has a dull finish.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, forming a whorl of approximately 5 leaves, visible in images 1, 2, and 4)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the apex of the shoot)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided blades)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): toothed (fine, regular serrations are visible along the leaf margins, especially in image 5)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are broadly oval with the widest point near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a distinct, elongated tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering gradually toward the petiole attachment)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): highly visible, evenly spaced, numerous (curving toward the leaf margin, creating a distinct reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (surface appears matte rather than glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible on the leaf surface, giving it a slightly textured appearance)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade size)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the visible stem appears soft and green, typical of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the stem, particularly near the leaf attachment points)
    19. Stem color: green
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): present (small, yellowish-green stipules are visible at the base of the petioles in images 1 and 5)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The plant exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the shoot apex. The leaves have a characteristic appearance with prominent, curved secondary veins and a finely toothed margin. The surface is covered in fine hairs and has a dull finish.
